title: The sacred months
hook: four sacred months: Muharram, Rajab, Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah (9:36)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the whole road of a life: carried, then carrying, then carried again. Your line: from call to prayer. When a bell or an alarm went off, did you check what your hands were carrying? Today, a new stretch: the year itself. Day one thousand three hundred fifty-three.

The verse begins by counting. Surah al-Tawbah, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! the number of the months with Allah is twelve months by Allah's ordinance in the day that He created the heavens and the earth." A calendar, built into creation. Then it marks some of the months off from the others: "Four of them are sacred." It doesn't name them. For the names, you have to go to a sermon the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, gave at the farewell pilgrimage. So this new stretch of the path, the festival year, starts with a question: which four, and what makes a month sacred?
screen: `TWELVE MONTHS WITH ALLAH.` → `FOUR OF THEM ARE SACRED.` → `WHICH FOUR?`

segments.voice: Start with the names. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Abu Bakrah reports the Prophet's words at the farewell pilgrimage, in paraphrase: the year is twelve months, and four of them are sacred. Three come one after another: Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah and Muharram. And the fourth stands alone: Rajab, the one between Jumada and Sha'ban. So it's three in a row, and one on its own. Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah, Muharram. Then Rajab. Now the instruction that comes with them. Back in al-Tawbah, right after "Four of them are sacred," the verse says: "So wrong not yourselves in them." Notice who gets protected. Not the month. You. The harm the verse names is the harm a person does to themselves, and some commentators read it as saying that wrongdoing weighs heavier in these months, the way a careless word lands harder in a holy place. That's the third idea: sacred time works like sacred space. A mosque is still a building, with walls and a floor. But you walk in differently. These four months are still ordinary weeks, with work and errands and laundry. But the calendar says: walk in differently. Be slower to quarrel. Quicker to do good. And the fourth idea is the gift of the pattern itself. Because the months are named and fixed, nobody has to decide each year when to be more careful. The calendar decides. You just notice when you've crossed the threshold. Over the coming days, the path walks through the year: Muharram, then the other months Muslims keep, all the way to Ramadan and the Eids.
screen: `THREE IN A ROW, AND RAJAB ALONE.` · `SO WRONG NOT YOURSELVES IN THEM.` · `SACRED TIME, LIKE SACRED SPACE.` · `THE CALENDAR DECIDES FOR YOU.`

segments.voice: The practice: learn the four. Settle, and breathe. On each slow breath, say one name, silently or out loud. Dhul Qa'dah. Dhul Hijjah. Muharram. Then pause, because there's a gap in the calendar, and say the last one: Rajab. Go round again, three and a pause and one, until the shape feels familiar. Then, for the rest of the sit, think of one place where you already walk in differently, a room, a grave, a kitchen table, and let the four months feel like that place. The bell holds the time.
The sacred months. Four of the twelve, named in the farewell sermon: Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab on its own. Times not to wrong yourselves. Today's word.

Your line: four sacred months. Today, look up where the Islamic calendar is right now, and see how far away the next sacred month is. Tomorrow, Muharram: the month of Allah. Day one thousand three hundred fifty-three.

screen: `DAY 1353 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: MUHARRAM: THE MONTH OF ALLAH.`

howItsDone: The Islamic calendar treats Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab as sacred months, named in a hadith of the farewell sermon in al-Bukhari; Qur'an 9:36 asks people not to wrong themselves in them.

fork.setup: the verse has just said four months are sacred. what instruction comes next?
fork.reveal: al-Tawbah 9:36 continues: "So wrong not yourselves in them." the instruction protects the person, not the month.

trapdoor: what you thought: the sacred months are holidays.
what it means: four of the twelve months, ordinary weeks where a person is asked to walk in differently and not wrong themselves.
what a scholar hears: 9:36's "so wrong not yourselves in them," with the names supplied by Abu Bakrah's report of the farewell sermon, three in a row and Rajab alone.

sources.quoted: Lo! the number of the months with Allah is twelve months by Allah's ordinance in the day that He created the heavens and the earth. Four of them are sacred … So wrong not yourselves in them.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4662 (Abu Bakrah: the farewell sermon names the four sacred months)

notes: Confirm Pickthall's exact wording of 9:36 for the quoted parts.
Confirm Bukhari 4662 numbering and that it names Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah, Muharram, and 'Rajab of Mudar' between Jumada and Sha'ban.
The reading that wrongdoing 'weighs heavier' in the sacred months is attributed only to 'some commentators'; confirm it is a fair summary of the tafsir tradition (e.g. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah).
The index lists the months as Muharram, Rajab, Dhul Qa'dah, Dhul Hijjah; the script follows the hadith's order.
